long_biography.plain_text:
Responsibility for a multigenerational wine house came to Philippe Sereys de Rothschild after two predecessors had reshaped it. His grandfather introduced château bottling, developed branded wine and secured First Growth status for Mouton. His mother broadened the portfolio and its international reach. Their example frames his stewardship of a business where agriculture, brands and art remain deliberately linked.

Before taking on the family company, Sereys de Rothschild worked on mergers and acquisitions at Lazard, managed environmental and energy operations, led a software company and invested in private equity. He later helped establish a champagne venture shared across Rothschild family branches. That outside experience gives his work a dual character: preserving a celebrated agricultural institution while directing a modern international drinks business.
